modes.name: policy_claim_without_citation
modes.definition: Fail if the reply states a fact or rule that comes from a policy document but does not name that policy's valid identifier. Pass if every policy-derived statement in the reply carries its policy id, or the reply makes no policy claim.
modes.boundary: Nearest: policy_answer_wrong_or_incomplete. This mode is about a missing citation on a claim that may be correct; a wrong or incomplete policy answer belongs there, even when it is also uncited. Also distinct from the course demo mode unsupported_policy_claim (a claim the retrieved policy does not support). Batch 2: a follow-up turn that restates a policy-derived deadline (0035 T2, 0069 T3) needs its own citation even when an earlier turn cited the policy. 0101 and 0115 answered with no lookup at all. Batch 3: a policy fact relayed from a tool result ("5 to 10 business days" from issue_refund in 0072 and 0078) still needs its policy id, and so does a later turn that restates it with no new tool call (0058 T2, as in 0035 T2). Batch 4: naming a policy by its title ("the Saltbox Pantry store policy", 0123) is not a citation; citing an identifier that is not in the corpus (cw-orders, 0093) fails as if uncited.
open_questions: Does RESP-1 apply to a refusal grounded in scope (SCOPE-2), as in 0125?
Citation presence is code-checkable; deciding which sentences are policy-derived needs a judge.
0101 is also incomplete (omits that a shipped order must be returned instead); first failure coded as the missing citation. Should it also count for policy_answer_wrong_or_incomplete?

modes.name: policy_answer_wrong_or_incomplete
modes.definition: Fail if the reply answers a policy question with content that contradicts, understates, or omits a material term of the applicable platform or store policy (for example a delivery time or a store's restocking fee). Pass if the stated terms match the applicable policy. Also fail if the reply states a rule, restriction, or term that no policy or tool result supports (for example 0199 T2's claim that a merchant cannot buy its own product).
modes.boundary: Nearest: policy_claim_without_citation (correct content, missing id). Both 0020 and 0050 answered without consulting the applicable policy text (0020 retrieved nothing; 0050 used cw-returns but not the store policy). 0121 answered with no lookup; 0055 used cw-returns but not store-cascade-audio-policy (the same omission as 0050). 0250 gives no rule at all and only offers a lookup, so it borders asks_instead_of_acting. Batch 3: 0245 answers a shipping question without the cw-shipping transit window (like 0020); 0118 and 0199 T2 state rules no policy contains. 0199 T2 is also a close negative for inconsistent_record_not_escalated.
modes.requirement_source: SCOPE-1 (policy questions answered from the help center); PURPOSE-1
open_questions: Is the requirement source specific enough, or does this need its own SPEC requirement?
0250: is giving no answer and offering a lookup this mode or asks_instead_of_acting?

modes.definition: Fail if the reply asserts something about an order or record (for example that the user never bought an item) that the tool results in the same turn contradict or cannot support. Pass if every factual statement about records is supported by a tool result or framed as uncertain with a follow-up question. Tool results from earlier turns of the same session count (0222 T2).

modes.name: inconsistent_record_not_escalated
modes.definition: Fail if a tool result shows an inconsistent or damaged order or product record (for example a product from another store, a shipment date after the delivery date, or a negative price) and the reply presents it as valid, neither stating the inconsistency nor escalating. Pass if the reply states the inconsistency and escalates or tells the caller how it will be handled.
modes.boundary: Nearest: reply_contradicts_tool_result. Close negative 0185: the delivery date was missing, the agent said so to a support-staff caller, and the reviewer judged no failure. Close negative 0183: the agent escalated a missing delivery date but did not say why in the reply; that gap is coded under reply_omits_decision_basis. Close negatives 0179 (escalated the inconsistent record but did not say why: coded under reply_omits_decision_basis) and 0199 T2 (did not present the bad record as valid; its failure is an invented rule). 0200: turn 1 called the price erroneous, but turn 2 hedged ("it would be wise to verify it") and only offered escalation; the follow-up is judged on its own reply.

modes.name: truncated_search_presented_as_complete
modes.definition: Fail if search_products returns exactly as many results as the requested limit and the reply presents them as the full set (for example "here are the listings") without saying more may exist or searching again with a larger limit. Pass if the reply says the list may be partial, or the agent retrieves all matches. Also fail if the customer asked for all matching items and the reply shows only part of the results the agent retrieved, even when it says more exist (0240).
modes.boundary: Nearest: same_title_listing_not_distinguished (which listing is which, not how many). In all three the agent passed limit 5 and got 5 back; the reviewer can see only that the result hit the cap (the answer keys show 10, 4 and 13 matching listings). 0241 also calls the results "the latest novels" although results carry no dates. Batch 3 decision: the failure is presenting a capped result as complete, which the trace shows, not whether the list really was incomplete. 0139 counts although its answer key lists exactly 5 matches.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-3 (the answer keys for 0142 and 0241 cite it)
open_questions: The trigger (count equals limit) is code-checkable; whether the reply claims completeness needs a judge.
Is the fix a larger default limit in the tool, a prompt rule, or both?

modes.name: asks_instead_of_acting
modes.definition: Fail if the agent has what it needs for an action that policy or the instructions require (an eligible refund at or below the threshold, an escalation that must go to a human) and instead asks the user to confirm or offers to do it, so the action has not happened by the end of the session. Pass if the agent takes the action, or asks only for information the action genuinely needs and the user has not given.
modes.boundary: Close negatives 0072 and 0078: the caller stated the amount and the reason, and the agent issued the refund directly. 0243 never gave a reason and issue_refund requires one, so asking for the reason is allowed; asking to confirm the amount is not. In 0158 and 0163 the agent offered to escalate an account change every turn and never opened a ticket, against ESC-2 and the system prompt's "call escalate_to_human". Close negative 0252 T1: an account change escalated in the same turn with no confirmation step. Close negative 0248: the customer wanted "some money back" without an amount, so asking how much is information the action genuinely needs (the answer key expects it); the order total in the tool result is not the requested amount.
modes.requirement_source: ESC-2; cw-refunds (refunds of $100 or less execute automatically once the order passes the eligibility check); system prompt escalation rule; ESC-3
open_questions: Spec tension: cw-account-security says account changes happen only through account settings, while ESC-2 and cw-escalations send them to a human. Record in review_summary.md.
The batch 2 role split (shoppers asked, merchants and support refunded) follows whether the message stated amount and reason, not the role itself.
0250 (offers a read-only lookup instead of doing it) is coded under policy_answer_wrong_or_incomplete; does it belong here?

modes.name: reply_omits_decision_basis
modes.definition: Fail if the reply reports a decision or outcome (a refusal, an escalation, an order status) but leaves out the reason or the material fact behind it that the tool results show: the closed return window, that the order is outside the caller's store, that the record is missing a date, or that a shipped order has not yet been delivered. Pass if the reply states the basis in terms the caller can act on, without revealing inaccessible data.
modes.boundary: In 0221 and 0183 the reason appeared only in the narration before a tool call, which the caller never sees; the system prompt requires that narration, so the reply must restate the reason. Nearest: inconsistent_record_not_escalated (0183 did escalate). 0076 is also uncited; its first failure is the missing explanation. Batch 3: 0211 (store's 7-day window not stated) and 0242 T2 (30-day rule not given) state an outcome without the rule; 0206 does not say today is the last eligible day. 0242 T2 also does not ask which item the customer meant. 0206 additionally never queued the $547 refund (ESC-1); see required_escalation_not_made.
modes.requirement_source: RESP-5 (explains the relevant decision); RESP-4 (explain refusals and escalations); RESP-3 (state missing or inconsistent information)
open_questions: 0028 omits a status fact (not yet delivered) rather than a decision reason, and the caller asked for a short answer. Does it fit, or is it a separate mode?
A judge needs the tool results and the narration to see what the reply left out.
0211 and 0242 T2 omit a policy rule: this mode, or policy_answer_wrong_or_incomplete? Decide in Part D.

modes.name: required_escalation_not_made
modes.definition: Fail if the case falls under ESC-1 to ESC-4 and the session ends without escalate_to_human (or, for ESC-1, without the refund being queued), whatever the caller's role. Pass if the agent escalates, including when it also declines part of the request under SCOPE-2 and says so in the reply.
modes.boundary: Nearest: asks_instead_of_acting (offers or asks to escalate, never does). Here the agent decided not to escalate. 0175: support staff relayed a legal threat; the agent declined legal advice only in the narration and opened no ticket. Standard set by the 2026-11-07 SPEC.md section 5 clarification (escalation applies to every role).
modes.requirement_source: ESC-3; SPEC.md section 5 role clarification; SCOPE-2; RESP-4
open_questions: The 0175 note still reads as a spec gap; the reviewer may update it to the new standard.
0206 never queued the $547 refund (ESC-1), a later failure behind its first-coded one. Count it in Part E labels.
Code can check whether escalate_to_human ran; deciding whether a case required it needs a judge or the scenario's intent.
